options.content:
# Ignite
Use this dashboard to monitor the Ignite data-grid service in this deployment. It provides visibility into cluster activity, memory and cache behavior, and operational health signals. Compare the affected node or cache with overall cluster trends to distinguish a localized resource issue from a broader cluster condition.

panels.description: Turn on debug logs on ignite to get details or tail the audit-log Kafka topic
panels.title: Discovery / Continuity Error Counters

panels.description: Metric records dropped for tenant/objectType with the reason for the drop
panels.title: Dropped record counts

panels.description: Error rate during normalization. Turn on debug logs on ignite to get details
panels.title: Normalization errors

options.content:
Each `ignite.$family.*` family shares one fixed **disk budget**, managed like **Linux memory watermarks**: data is retained and space is freed **only when usage approaches the budget**. Space is shared by *demand-weighted max-min fairness* — **busier topics are protected with a larger share** and no active topic is starved below a floor. When the budget is pressured the leader reclaims **already-consumed (oldest) bytes first — no data loss**, and only evicts *unprocessed* data as a last resort under pressure with `RETENTION_RECLAIM_ENABLED=true`. Note: `retention.bytes` is **per-partition** — topic cap = value × partitions.

> **How to read this section** — every panel's tooltip (ⓘ) explains what it shows, what good vs bad looks like, and how to fix a bad state. **Green = healthy, red = acting now / data at risk.** Top row = family health at a glance; middle = who holds the budget and the trend; lower = per-topic detail, reclaim activity, and allocator health. Use the **Family** dropdown to switch between `latent` and `contemporary`.

panels.description: How full the family's disk budget is (used ÷ budget). GOOD: < 85% (green) — plenty of headroom. WATCH: 85–95% (yellow) — approaching the watermark, lossless reclaim may begin. BAD: > 95% (red) — at capacity; unprocessed data will be evicted if inflow continues. FIX: raise `*_TOTAL_RETENTION_BYTES` if disk allows, and/or clear consumer lag so more bytes become reclaimable losslessly (see Consumer backlog panel).
panels.title: Budget Utilisation

panels.description: The budget (ceiling), current on-disk usage, and remaining headroom. GOOD: Free > 0 and Used comfortably below Budget. BAD: Free at/below 0 (red) — the family is over budget and reclaiming now. FIX: raise `*_TOTAL_RETENTION_BYTES` (needs disk) or reduce inflow; if Free is negative while lossy reclaim is 0, the allocator is holding the line by evicting already-consumed data (healthy).
panels.title: Budget / Used / Free

panels.description: Overall health of the family right now. GOOD: HEALTHY (green) — every topic's floor is guaranteed, normal operation; AT CAPACITY (orange) is also OK — the budget is full but only already-consumed data is being freed, with no data loss. WATCH: THIN (yellow) — there are more topics than the budget can fully reserve a floor for; harmless unless they all fill at once. BAD: SHEDDING (red) — unprocessed data is being deleted to protect the disk. FIX: SHEDDING → clear consumer lag (scale the Spark consumer) and/or raise the family budget `*_TOTAL_RETENTION_BYTES`; THIN → raise the budget, lower `*_TOPIC_FLOOR_BYTES`, or reduce `IGNITE_TOPIC_PARTITIONS`.
panels.title: Provisioning State

panels.description: Left — number of topics the controller manages: steady is normal, a sudden jump means topic churn. Right — Floor reservation = the sum of every topic's guaranteed floor as a percentage of the budget. GOOD: < 100% (green) — all floors fit inside the budget with room to spare. WATCH: ≥ 100% (yellow) — floors alone exceed the budget, so they become best-effort and simultaneous bursts could overflow. FIX (≥ 100%): raise `*_TOTAL_RETENTION_BYTES`, lower `*_TOPIC_FLOOR_BYTES`, or reduce `IGNITE_TOPIC_PARTITIONS` to shrink each topic's minimum.
panels.title: Topics & floor reservation
How it works — the control loop

options.content:
**Flow:** `Producers → ignite.$family.* topics → Spark consumer`, with a leader-only **controller** on the side.

Each cycle (default 5m) the controller:
1. **Measures** on-disk bytes per topic (`DescribeLogDirs`).
2. **Allocates** a fair share: a floor for every topic + demand-weighted surplus, capped by max-share so no topic hoards. Busier topics keep a bigger protected share.
3. **Applies** per-partition `retention.bytes` caps — raises eagerly, shrinks reluctantly.
4. **Reclaims only under pressure**, oldest-first: **already-consumed bytes first (no data loss)**, and *unprocessed* data only as a last resort when `RETENTION_RECLAIM_ENABLED=true`.

**Reading the dashboard:** _Budget Utilisation_ & _Provisioning State_ = is it healthy? _Top topics_ & the _per-topic table_ = who holds the budget. _Reclaim rate_ = is it losing data (red = yes). _Consumer backlog_ = the early warning. _Reconcile freshness / errors_ = is the controller itself alive.

panels.description: Trend of the three key lines: Budget (dashed ceiling), Provisioned = Σ of applied caps, and actual Used. GOOD: Used stays below Budget and Provisioned hugs the Budget line (≈ ×1.0). BAD: Used crossing/riding the Budget line = at capacity; Provisioned far above Budget = over-provisioned (thin). Watch for Used climbing steadily toward Budget — pressure is building. FIX: if Used is pinned at Budget, raise `*_TOTAL_RETENTION_BYTES` or reduce inflow; if Provisioned ≫ Budget, see the Topics & floor reservation panel.
panels.title: Budget vs Used over time

panels.description: Per-topic detail, sorted by utilisation. Columns: Used / Cap (its protected share), Utilisation = Used/Cap (gauge), Unconsumed = bytes not yet read by the Spark group, Evictable (consumed) = Used − Unconsumed (bytes that can be freed with NO data loss). GOOD: Utilisation < 0.8 (green) and Unconsumed small. WATCH: Utilisation 0.8–0.95 (yellow). BAD: Utilisation ≥ 0.95 (red) = saturated / about to evict; Unconsumed large and rising = that topic's consumer is falling behind (precursor to data loss). FIX: saturated-but-low-Unconsumed topics are safe (they reclaim consumed data); for large/rising Unconsumed, scale the Spark consumer — raising the budget only delays it.
panels.title: Per-topic retention budget

panels.description: Ranks the biggest consumers of the budget right now (on-disk bytes per topic, top 12). Use it to spot which object types dominate the family. GOOD: usage spread across several topics. BAD: one or two bars holding most of the budget — a single verbose object type (e.g. a backfill burst) is squeezing everyone else. FIX: if that topic is legitimately dominant and others are starved, raise `*_TOTAL_RETENTION_BYTES`; if it is a runaway, the max-share ceiling already caps it — confirm `RETENTION_MAX_TOPIC_SHARE_PCT` is set.
panels.title: Top topics by on-disk usage

panels.description: How often the controller rewrites caps, by direction: raise (give a topic more room — non-destructive), lower (return unused headroom), bound (budget-restoring clamp). GOOD: low and steady. BAD: a high sustained rate of 'lower' = caps flapping, which churns broker config and can trigger needless segment deletes. FIX for churn: increase `RETENTION_SHRINK_COOLDOWN` (debounce) and/or `RETENTION_MIN_CHANGE_PCT` (ignore small changes).
panels.title: Cap changes (raise / lower / bound)

panels.description: The single most important health signal: what kind of data is being freed. Lossless (green) deletes only already-consumed oldest segments — safe, expected background activity. Lossy (red) evicts UNPROCESSED data = real data loss. GOOD: lossy flat at 0 (any amount of green is fine). BAD: any sustained red — the family is shedding unprocessed data. FIX: (1) clear consumer lag — scale the Spark consumer; (2) raise `*_TOTAL_RETENTION_BYTES` if disk allows; (3) confirm `RETENTION_RECLAIM_ENABLED=true` is intended (this is the deliberate 'protect the disk, lose some data' path).
panels.title: Reclaim rate — lossless vs lossy

panels.description: The leading indicator of trouble — it rises BEFORE the budget fills and before any data loss. Per-topic bytes on disk that the designated Spark group (latent→latentapp, contemporary→streamingapp) has NOT yet read, scoped to the selected $family. GOOD: low and flat/declining (and 0 when the family has no data) — the consumer keeps up, so almost all on-disk data is reclaimable losslessly. BAD: a steady climb — Spark is falling behind; that data cannot be reclaimed safely, so continued inflow will force lossy eviction. FIX: scale/repair the Spark consumer for this family; raising the budget only buys time. (Raw kafka-exporter `kafka_consumergroup_lag_sum` is deliberately NOT mixed in here because its group name does not follow the family label — add it in a separate panel if you need message-count lag.)
panels.title: Consumer backlog (unconsumed bytes, per $family)

panels.description: Seconds since the controller last completed a cycle — the classic sawtooth: it climbs, then drops back to ~0 each time a reconcile finishes. GOOD: teeth peak below one reconcile interval and keep dropping (controller alive and enforcing the budget). BAD: the line climbs past the dashed lines (900s warn / 1800s crit) without dropping — the allocator is stuck, there is no elected leader, or `DescribeLogDirs` is failing, so caps are no longer being updated. FIX: check the Allocator errors panel and the Ignite leader-pod logs, and verify Kafka admin connectivity.
panels.title: Time since last reconcile

panels.description: p95 duration of one controller cycle. GOOD: a few seconds — far below the reconcile interval (default 5m). BAD: climbing toward the interval = the loop can't finish in time (too many topics, slow Kafka admin), which delays cap updates and budget enforcement. FIX: investigate Kafka admin/broker latency; consider a longer `IGNITE_RETENTION_RECONCILE_INTERVAL`, or reduce the topic/partition count for the family.
panels.title: Reconcile duration (p95)

panels.description: Kafka admin-API failures by operation. GOOD: flat 0. BAD: any sustained rate — the controller can't do its job: describe_log_dirs = can't measure usage; alter_config = can't apply caps; consumer_offsets = can't read committed offsets (so data is treated as unconsumed and lossless reclaim shrinks to ~0). FIX: check Kafka broker/admin connectivity and permissions; for consumer_offsets verify the group names `RETENTION_LATENT_CONSUMER_GROUP` / `RETENTION_CONTEMPORARY_CONSUMER_GROUP` exist and commit offsets.
panels.title: Allocator errors

panels.description: Health of BOTH families over time — the at-a-glance incident history. GOOD: mostly green (HEALTHY); orange (AT CAPACITY) is acceptable — budget full but no data loss. WATCH: yellow (THIN). BAD: any red (SHEDDING) — unprocessed data was deleted at that time; correlate with the Reclaim rate and Consumer backlog panels. FIX: red → scale the Spark consumer and/or raise `*_TOTAL_RETENTION_BYTES`; persistent yellow → raise the budget, lower `*_TOPIC_FLOOR_BYTES`, or reduce `IGNITE_TOPIC_PARTITIONS`.
panels.title: Provisioning state over time (latent vs contemporary)

panels.description: How much space can be freed safely per topic = already-consumed bytes (used − unconsumed), biggest first. This is the headroom the controller reclaims first when the budget is pressured, with NO data loss. GOOD: large green bars = plenty of safe headroom, so pressure can be relieved without evicting unprocessed data. BAD: bars near zero across the board = almost everything on disk is still unconsumed, so any further pressure forces lossy eviction — a consumer problem, not a disk problem. FIX: if bars are small and the budget is full, scale the Spark consumer so more data becomes reclaimable. (Note: the safest victim is the topic with the MOST disk and the LEAST unconsumed data — a high-lag topic is a poor victim, since evicting it would drop unprocessed records.)

targets.expr: sort_desc(topk(12, clamp_min(sum by (objectType) (ignite_retention_topic_used_bytes{family=~"$family", objectType=~"$objectType"}) - sum by (objectType) (ignite_retention_topic_unconsumed_bytes{family=~"$family", objectType=~"$objectType"}), 0)))

panels.title: Reclaimable headroom per topic (already-consumed, safe to free)
